threads.body: Please qualify this checklist with which variants the instrumented API actually supports. The current instruction requires reviewers to flag every changed method lacking sync, async, streaming, or early-close tests, including methods with no streaming or async counterpart. That produces false-positive findings and contradicts section 6's existing “when both exist” qualification. Apply the checklist only to supported variants and applicable content/error paths.

threads.body: Signature inspection can be cached, but `Signature.bind(*args, **kwargs)` must run for each invocation because it binds that call's actual arguments. This wording would flag correct implementations such as LangChain's `_run_context.py:247–257`, which caches the signature and binds inside the wrapper. Please distinguish signature inspection from per-call argument binding.

@@ -4,6 +4,96 @@ applyTo: "instrumentation/**"
 
 Review rules for PRs touching `instrumentation/**`. Flag violations with a link to the rule.
 
+## Top checks
+
+Go through these on every PR before the detailed sections below.
+
+**Tests.** For every new or changed instrumented method, list which of these are missing and flag
+the PR: sync | async | streaming | provider error | stream closed early | content capture on |
+content capture off (content absent).
+- For a fix or behavior change, flag tests that would pass without it (no assertion on the
+  changed value). Tests that only add coverage are fine. Flag presence/length/substring checks
+  instead of exact values.
+- Flag tests that call `_private` helpers or hand-built SDK mocks instead of the instrumented
+  client public API.
+
+**Types and speculative code.**
+- Flag `Any`/`object` in signatures and `getattr`/`hasattr` on known SDK types. Flag reads of
+  fields, params, or methods that don't exist in every supported library version, and guards for
+  cases the library never produces.
+  ```python
+  # Flag
+  def _set_response(inv, response: Any) -> None:
+      inv.response_model_name = getattr(response, "model", None)
+
+
+  # Prefer
+  def _set_response(inv: InferenceInvocation, response: ChatCompletion) -> None:
+      inv.response_model_name = response.model
+  ```
+
+**Semconv values.**
+- Flag `gen_ai.provider.name` fallbacks other than `unknown` (e.g. the framework name),
+  `gen_ai.agent.id` set from a local object id or name, finish reasons defaulted instead of
+  mapped, and spans/metric points emitted per retry.
+- Flag sampling-relevant values (agent name, conversation id) set after the `handler.*()` call.
+
+**Values and finalization.**
+- Flag `x or default` / `if x:` on numeric or boolean telemetry values, and placeholder `''`/`0`
+  for missing values.
+  ```python
+  # Flag
+  inv.temperature = kwargs.get("temperature") or None
+  # Prefer
+  if (temperature := kwargs.get("temperature")) is not None:
+      inv.temperature = temperature
+  ```
+- Flag code paths that start an invocation without reaching `stop()`/`fail()`.
+
+**Messages and content.**
+- Flag `json.dumps`/`str()` results assigned to util message or tool fields,
+  `TextPart(content=str(block))` or `GenericPart` for non-text blocks, and branches that
+  silently drop block types the library documents.
+- Flag message parts, tool definitions, or streamed text built when content capture is disabled.
+- Flag any deprecated util API (e.g. `LLMInvocation`, deprecated part aliases or fields), such as `GenericPart` and `get_telemetry_handler()`.
+
+**Versions.**
+- Flag patches of optional or version-specific symbols that break `instrument()` or uninstrument
+  when the symbol is missing, patches applied to re-exporting modules instead of the defining
+  class, and version-specific branches no `oldest`/`latest` test reaches.
+
+**Performance.** Flag per-call work that can run once at instrument time (imports, signature
+binding, feature checks), per-chunk stream processing that re-joins or re-parses everything
+accumulated so far, and blocking work on async code paths.

threads.body: `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons` is Recommended, not Required, in the inference semantic conventions, and the util omits an empty list. Using it as the required-list example directs contributors to retain an attribute the util suppresses. Remove this example and defer required-list handling to the relevant attribute's conventions.

@@ -159,13 +176,66 @@ Follow [Streaming responses](../util/opentelemetry-util-genai/AGENTS.md#streamin
 `SyncStreamWrapper` / `AsyncStreamWrapper`, call `invocation.suspend()` before returning the stream,
 and don't call `invocation.stop()` when the SDK returns the stream.
 
+### Context propagation
+
+- When the instrumented call returns, its span must not be current in the caller's context, on
+  any path: streams (including tool streams), raw or unparsed responses, early returns. Suspend or
+  detach before returning.
+- For async APIs, start the invocation inside the awaited coroutine, not when the coroutine is
+  created. Otherwise concurrent calls nest under each other.
+- Don't suppress context detach errors. They signal mismatched attach/detach; fix the pairing.
+
+## Library versions
+
+- If a symbol you patch is optional or only exists in some supported versions, skip that patch
+  when it's missing - and skip it on uninstrument too. One missing symbol must not break
+  `instrument()` for the rest of the library.
+- Patch the class or function where it's defined, not a module that re-exports it, so the patch
+  doesn't depend on import order.
+- Avoid patching private library internals. When you must, check them against the oldest and
+  latest supported versions.
+- Every version-specific branch needs a test that runs in the `oldest` or `latest` env. A test
+  that is skipped in both is not coverage.
+
+## Performance
+
+Instrumentation runs on every call of the instrumented library.
+
+- Resolve imports, signatures, and feature checks once at instrument or import time, not per call.
+- Keep per-chunk stream processing O(1): append chunks and join or parse once at the end.
+- Don't block the event loop or move work onto it from async code paths.
+
+## Common bugs
+
+- Use `is not None` for optional values. `or` and truthiness checks drop valid `0`, `0.0`, and
+  `False`.
+- Don't invent `'unknown'`, `''`, or `0` for missing optional attributes - leave them unset,
+  unless semconv defines a fallback value (e.g. `unknown` for `gen_ai.provider.name`). Omit
+  optional list attributes when empty; required ones (e.g. `gen_ai.response.finish_reasons`) are
+  still recorded.

threads.body: As written, this suppresses distinct nested operations, such as tools invoked by agents and application-defined subgraphs, rather than just duplicate wrapper layers. The [agent semantic conventions](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai/blob/main/docs/gen-ai/gen-ai-agent-spans.md) explicitly recommend reporting application-defined workflows even when nested. Limit outer-span suppression to entry points representing the same logical operation, preserving distinct child operations and independent batch items.

 - **No** → don't emit a workflow span. A single agent run or a plain chain of calls is not an AI
   workflow.
 
+### One span per operation
+
+- When one wrapped entry point calls another wrapped one in the same library (e.g. `run` calls
+  `run_async`, or a batch API calls the single-item API), emit only the outer span. Test nested
+  and threaded topologies for duplicate spans.

threads.body: The util's message-level `FinishReason` literal contains `tool_call`, while the OpenAI response extractor test expects `tool_calls` for the span attribute (`test_response_extractors.py:1201`). Requiring that literal would incorrectly normalize valid span finish reasons. Follow the span attribute's semantic conventions instead of constraining it to the message-level literal.
